correctness.rationale: Block diagonalization gives the exact nuclear norm sqrt((1+t)^2-4ta). Signed cumulative differences of two k-point equal-unit-weight empirical measures have at most k-1 sign changes. A strictly positive Wronskian yields a matching Chebyshev test function that contradicts the k zero moments unless the measures coincide. The Jacobian of any m<k evaluations has full rank m on the chamber of distinct interior angles, so IFT supplies genuine inequivalent counterexamples for every shorter prescribed sample list. Endpoint and multiplicity cases and quantifiers were checked. 950 finite diagnostic assertions passed; they are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Recent Grassmannian Schatten-isometry work proves one-scale formulas and rigidity of isometry maps, not arbitrary-scale finite trace norm inverse tomography. The exact equal-weight k-sample recovery plus universal sharp k-1 nonidentification are not in located primary or published-finding corpus items. value.rationale: A complete and sharp minimal-number classification for an intrinsic family of invariants: exactly k fixed nuclear-norm queries recover all k principal angles for arbitrary rank-k projection pairs, while any m<k fixed queries fail even generically. This fills a natural identifiability gap between canonical-angle structure and numerical Schatten-distance measurements. Hilbert-Schmidt pencils exhibit a contrasting permanent collapse to one scalar. No finite table or arbitrary narrow slice is used.
